title: Environmental Contaminants in Biota
abstract: Discussing the interpretation of tissue concentrations of contaminants in wildlife, this updated edition of a bestseller draws on current scientific research and includes new chapters and greater emphasis on aquatic organisms. Each chapter provides a summary and review of a specific chemical along with direction on research methods and the interpretation of conflicting or insufficient data. Chapters include a comprehensive history of contaminant interpretation in wildlife and fish, the use of tissue residues in ecological risk assessment, and detailed coverage of all bioaccumulative contaminants and their physiologic affects.

narrative:
Short impact summary

Environmental Contaminants in Biota (2011), published by Taylor & Francis, has been cited 972 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 1% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it has been downloaded 992 times.

Full narrative

Environmental Contaminants in Biota by W. Nelson Bey and James P. Meador was published by Taylor & Francis in 2011. Conceptually, the work connects to Biota, Contamination, Environmental science, Environmental chemistry and Chemistry.

OpenAlex records 972 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2011 with 67 citing works. Notable citing venues include The Science of The Total Environment, Archives of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology and Environmental Pollution. The citing works include 859 journal articles, 61 book chapters, 22 dissertations and 11 reports. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, Canada and Spain.

It has been downloaded 992 times via OAPEN. Open Library reports a combined count of 5 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Life below water among the Sustainable Development Goals.
